svg.text: If you run a node: what the devnet says to budget
measured on pbt-devnet-1 · 3.55 B leaves, about a fifth more than mainnet's state · 16 GiB nodes unless stated
memory
16 GiB worked on every client; 32 GB (EIP-7870's full node) is comfortable. An import peaks in its replay:
Nethermind's sat at 97 % of 16 GiB.
disk
peak datadir 1.4–1.8 TiB for a self-conversion, chain history included; an import adds the 163 GB package. The fork
gives 220–380 GiB back (geth, Besu).
writes
507–2,516 GiB written per migration: plan the SSD's endurance, not its size.
time
self-conversion 2h41m–5h01m to the head; snapshot import 3h59m–6h03m, of which 1–4 h is replaying the week since the
anchor.
CPU
3–5 of 16 cores busy while building, about one afterwards; the disk under half busy. Not the constraint.
steps
1 get the preimage file for the anchor · 2 start the client with its conversion flag · 3 it scans its own state,
builds and verifies the tree (check 2 where the client has it) · 4 it replays the blocks produced meanwhile · 5 two
trees until the fork · 6 the MPT is disposed after the fork finalizes.
watch for
memory during the replay; a restart during the window needs a persisted post-fork state (fixed in geth after the
devnet); do not keep import flags across the fork.
